name: Haggi
overview: Haggi is a male member of the tribe of Gad, known as the son of Gad. He is listed among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, indicating his place within the early patriarchal family during the time of Israel's descent into Egypt. His descendants are associated with the Haggites mentioned in the book of Numbers.
namesAndTitles: The name Haggi means 'festal' or 'born on the feast day,' reflecting a possible connection to a significant religious celebration. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Haggi as a son of Gad, establishing his immediate family connection. No other family relationships beyond this are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Haggi's significance lies in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who migrated to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational lineage of the Israelite nation during a pivotal moment in their history. His descendants, the Haggites, are noted in the census of the tribe of Gad, indicating the continuation of his family line within the tribal structure of Israel. This situates Haggi within the broader narrative of God's covenant people and their growth as a nation.
